verbs.name: system.doctor
verbs.description: Scan the runtime environment and return structured CAPABILITY CARDS — the single source of truth the start wizard, Settings, and any agent over REST/MCP all read (the shellX 'provider model card' pattern, applied to ShellX Cut's own deps). Cards: ffmpeg + ffprobe (resolved path, source rung env|bundled-or-appdata|path|missing via the cut-media toolpath ladder, version from `<tool> -version`, runnable flag, a platform-specific hint when missing, and details.setup = {route: builtin_download|homebrew|package_manager, fetch_available, steps[], commands[{label, command}], help_url, custom_build, download?: {publisher, publisher_url, version, size_bytes, size_is_exact, license, license_url, source_url, limitation, consent}} (steps/commands are the other way when a download exists, e.g. Homebrew on Apple silicon): the same setup guide the engine's tool_missing refusals point to; a refresh notices an ffmpeg installed or chosen since the last scan without restarting Cut); gpu-encode (details.ffmpeg_missing:true when no ffmpeg exists at all: nothing can export yet); perception (python interpreter via the sidecar ladder + a TIER: none|instruments-capable|full-stt, probed cheaply with a short timeout; details.installation records state:not_installed|ready|damaged, installation_id, python, version and the original probe error; a configured or previously recorded installation that cannot run is degraded with a repair reason, not a missing optional install); judge rungs claude|codex|antigravity|grok (details.found reports CLI resolution, while details.judge_ready admits that provider to render review; details.availability_reason is a string when unready and null when ready, and details.adapter_runtime_ready reports whether the bundled adapter and Python were available. Admission runs the bundled ladder's bounded no-model detect protocol and is never inferred from found/version. For Codex direct-frame review, the image/schema and tool-free capability check must pass before details.judge_ready can be true; Antigravity remains unready for render judging. A failed or malformed probe is status:unknown, not ready. details.chat remains the separate Agent Chat capability/session state); disk (free bytes on the app-data tools volume — downloads need it); plus os/arch/app_version/addr. The result is CACHED in server state, the scan runs once at startup, and a `doctor_updated` WS event fires whenever it changes (refresh / a completed fetch_tool). The ESSENTIAL gate is the ffmpeg card: when it is missing the first-run wizard surfaces; non-essentials never block the editor. Each card: {id, kind: tool|perception|judge|disk, status: ok|missing|degraded|unknown, source?, version?, hint?, details}. The ffmpeg card also has details.version_advice: null, or {in_use, tested_versions: [string], message, upgrade} when its readable major version is below 7; this is optional upgrade advice, leaves status and essential_ok unchanged, and preserves a manually chosen FFmpeg.

refresh.description: Re-scan instead of returning the cached report (default false — the cached read is fast and never blocks the verb loop; refresh re-probes ffmpeg/python/judge and re-emits doctor_updated on change).

feature.description: A verb name or feature id: what it needs and whether it can run now, without calling it. Returns only that answer: {verb?, feature, feature_name, can_run: yes|no|depends, requires: [{id, name, state, reason?, check?, get?}], any_of?, optional: [{id, name, state, effect}], blocked_by, depends_on, note?}.

verbs.result: DoctorReport {schema: "shellx-cut/doctor/1", scanned_at, os, arch, app_version, addr, cards: Card[], essential_ok, availability: {pause, camera, live_timer, microphone_choice, source_preview, managed_motion}, requirements} — availability contains fixed booleans for this system and executable, computed without listing, opening or asking permission for any device. It describes support, not setup/readiness; all six facts stay fixed while this engine runs. Older engines omit availability: treat missing fields as unknown, never false. essential_ok=false ⇒ ffmpeg missing ⇒ the wizard should surface. requirements (schema/requirements.json, the one registry of what needs what): {schema: "shellx-cut/requirements/1", tools: [{id, kind: tool|condition, name, what, state: ready|missing|needs_attention|not_checked|per_asset|not_applicable, reason?, check?: {verb, args}, get: {settings?, button?, verb?, args?, person?}, doctor_card?, license?: {name, url?}, needed_for: [feature names], improves: [feature names where it is optional], per_asset?}], features: [{id, name, verbs, requires, open_project: all|some|none, any_of?, verb_extra?, optional: [{id, name, state, effect}], can_run: yes|no|depends, blocked_by: [requirement with state, reason and get], depends_on, note?}]}. Tool states are read from these cards; screen, microphone and system-sound permission are not probed here (check names screen_record.doctor); a transcript or analysis is per asset. For uninstalled matte_premium, details.setup_supported is false only for the known dropped sm_70 generation, null when unknown/unqueried, otherwise the generation is admitted for setup (not a readiness claim). Its hint explains a refusal before downloading; an already installed older runtime retains its own readiness. With feature: only the answer for that verb or feature (see the feature argument).

verbs.name: system.motion_status
verbs.description: Run Cut's bounded, read-only ShellX Motion discovery route. It validates the local runtime probe, connector catalog, and fixed Template-to-Cut descriptor without a caller id, provider login, connector execution, download, installation, repair, update, or removal. A discovered runtime remains explicitly unmanaged and connector execution remains unqualified. Distribution lifecycle operations are unavailable until MOTION-DIST-01 provides a verified immutable distribution manifest and a matching platform artifact; no source checkout, PATH binary, or npm package is treated as an install candidate.

verbs.name: system.set_stt_model
verbs.description: Pick the TRANSCRIPTION (speech-to-text) model + optional language. Persists the choice in the perception app-data dir so every perception run injects it (SHELLX_CUT_STT_MODEL / SHELLX_CUT_STT_LANG) into the python sidecar. RECOMMENDED models: 'nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3' (~25 European languages, fast, torch-free, native WORD timestamps — THE DEFAULT, used for transcript cutting, kinetic captions, chapters), 'nemo-canary-1b-v2' (better accuracy for smaller/weak languages such as Latvian, with torchaudio MMS_FA forced alignment to produce WORD timestamps), and 'whisperx-large-v3' (compatibility fallback). Any onnx-asr / whisperx id is accepted (advanced) and downloads on first use. Omit `model` (or pass clear:true) to RESET to the default. The choice applies to the NEXT uncached perception run — re-run media.perception / media.transcribe on an asset (or re-import) to re-transcribe with it. system.doctor's perception card reports the active model.

model.description: The STT model id (e.g. 'nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3' for fast captions, 'nemo-canary-1b-v2' for smaller-language accuracy, or 'whisperx-large-v3' for fallback). Omit (or clear:true) to reset to the default.

language.description: Optional language hint (e.g. 'lv', 'de', 'fr', 'es'). Weak-language auto routing uses Canary + MMS_FA when no model is explicitly selected; Whisper fallback also uses the hint. Omit for auto.

clear.description: Reset to the built-in default model (ignores model/language).

verbs.name: system.set_ffmpeg
verbs.description: Set or clear the user's MANUAL ffmpeg choice (Settings > Video & performance > Video processing > Choose ffmpeg…). `path` = an absolute path to the ffmpeg executable the user picked; it is VALIDATED here (must answer `ffmpeg -version`) before being persisted to a small file beside the app-data tools dir, and it WINS over auto-selection. Omit `path` (or pass null) to CLEAR the override and go back to automatic (the best hardware-capable installed ffmpeg). The chosen build must have an ffprobe beside it (used for media inspection) unless one already resolves elsewhere; otherwise the call is refused with invalid_args before anything is saved. The choice applies at once: the doctor re-scans, re-probes the hardware encoders of the new build and fires doctor_updated, so restart_required is false (the field is kept for older clients). An explicit SHELLX_CUT_FFMPEG env var still takes precedence over this.

path.description: Absolute path to the chosen ffmpeg executable; null/omitted clears the override (back to automatic).

verbs.result: {override: string|null (the persisted choice after this call), restart_required: false, doctor: DoctorReport (rescanned)}

verbs.name: system.fetch_tool
verbs.description: Consented download + install of a MISSING runtime tool, as a background job (returns {job_id}; progress via the jobs domain + job_progress events). CONSENT (ffmpeg): nothing is downloaded unless accept_license is true; without it the verb answers ok:false, code invalid_args, with the exact consent text in error.cause (publisher, version or size, licence, source): show it to the person and call again with accept_license:true only when they agree (a person's own request for the download is that agreement); never agree without them. Built-in registry ids only, no caller URL; https only (redirects too) with deadlines. tool "ffmpeg" (consent also at the doctor's ffmpeg card details.setup.download.consent): Windows and Linux x86_64 get FFmpeg 9.0.2 (n9.0.2-39-g7adfbe40dc) from FFmpeg-Builds (release autobuild-2026-10-31-12-59, github.com/FFmpeg-Builds/FFmpeg-Builds), pinned by URL, size and SHA-256 of the archive and of ffmpeg/ffprobe; the zip must hold no link, absolute or .. path, only those two programs are unpacked and each must be a PE x64 / ELF x86-64 program; Windows on ARM gets the x64 build. macOS on Apple silicon: Martin Riedl's FFmpeg 9.0.2 (ffmpeg.martin-riedl.de; ffmpeg.zip + ffprobe.zip) pinned by version, size and SHA-256, one regular file per zip, a thin arm64 program whose signature verifies against the publisher's Developer ID (Team KU3N25YGLU); it has no vid.stab (Stabilize then needs Homebrew's ffmpeg-full; the job result's limitation says so). Checks run in a private temporary folder; only a verified payload moves into the app-data tools dir; a failed check installs nothing and names the check and the platform's options (retry; Homebrew on a Mac; the publisher's page on Windows; the distribution's package on Linux; or system.set_ffmpeg). Other platforms: ok:false, code unsupported_platform, no job. tool "vc-runtime" (Windows only; doctor card vc-runtime): Microsoft's Visual C++ Redistributable, which captions and the other Python features need. No accept_license: ask the person before downloading it and accepting Microsoft's licence (card details.license_name, details.license_url). Downloaded from Microsoft's permalink (aka.ms/vc14/vc_redist.x64.exe or vc_redist.arm64.exe, listed at learn.microsoft.com/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist) and run only after Windows' signature check accepts it as signed by Microsoft Corporation with a chain to a Microsoft root; started with /install /passive /norestart (visible progress), Windows then asks the PERSON for administrator permission (an agent cannot approve it). A failed job says why: the prompt was declined, this account cannot approve it (ask an administrator), the download failed or the signature check failed, each with Microsoft's page. On success the doctor re-scans (no restart) and doctor_updated fires. rationale is recorded on the job.

tool.description: Built-in registry id: "ffmpeg" (ffmpeg + ffprobe) or "vc-runtime" (Windows: Microsoft's Visual C++ Redistributable). Unknown ids fail fast; there is no URL arg.

accept_license.description: ffmpeg only: true only after the person agreed to the offer (doctor ffmpeg card details.setup.download.consent; also in error.cause when missing). Required for ffmpeg: without it nothing is downloaded. Not used for vc-runtime.

verbs.result: {job_id, tool} — watch job_progress or poll jobs.status. ffmpeg result: {tool, installed_dir, version, sha256 (one per archive, space-separated), source_url, bytes, ffmpeg_ok_after, limitation}. vc-runtime result: {installed, version, restart_needed, installer_exit_code, signer, source_url, bytes, sha256} (or {installed:true, already_installed:true}). doctor_updated fires on completion

verbs.name: system.setup_perception
verbs.description: Consented provisioning of the Python PERCEPTION venv (transcription + silence/scenes/beats + auto-reframe), as a background job (returns {job_id}; progress via the jobs domain + job_progress events). The installer ships only the sidecar SCRIPT (instruments.py + dependency requirements); this builds the heavy venv on first run, with consent. SECURITY (path-fencing model, same model as system.fetch_tool): it downloads `uv` (Astral's static Python provisioner) ONLY through the built-in fetch allow-list (version-pinned astral-sh/uv 0.13.9 release, per-archive SHA-256 embedded in Cut and verified before use) — NO caller-supplied URL. It then has uv install a standalone CPython 3.12 (system python is too old on real desktops — macOS ships 3.9, below the onnx-asr ≥3.10 floor), create the app-data sidecar venv, and `uv pip install -r` the BUNDLED requirements (onnx-asr Parakeet/Canary STT, torchaudio MMS_FA alignment, and the perception stack). On success the doctor re-scans and the `perception` card flips missing→ok. rationale is recorded on the job.

warm_model.description: Download and load the selected ONNX speech model after final dependency checks (default true; Parakeet v3 if no model is selected). Persisted model selection takes precedence over inherited environment. An explicit Whisper choice skips ONNX preparation and uses its own runtime on first transcription. model_warmed reports a successful load; model_warm_error preserves preparation failure separately from package installation. Set false to skip model preparation.

verbs.result: {job_id} — watch job_progress (downloading uv → installing Python → creating venv → installing dependencies → downloading model) or poll jobs.status; the job result is {venv_python, managed_python, python_version, uv_version, package_versions, onnx_asr_ready, model_warmed, model_warm_error, installation_record_error, full_perception_ready, extras_note, perception_ok_after}; failed model preparation or installation-record persistence completes with warnings while preserving installed dependencies; installation_record_error retains the supplemental metadata error and never invalidates the installed tools; doctor_updated fires on completion

verbs.name: system.setup_matte
verbs.description: Make AI BACKGROUND REMOVAL (edit.matte) usable LOCALLY — the seamless, one-click install of the user-side matte runtime (the ffmpeg pattern; the user NEVER runs pip or sees a terminal). With a prepared native runtime, reports its RVM readiness without downloading and refuses model-path overrides or MatAnyone2. Otherwise, with NO args: DOWNLOAD the 14 MB RVM model (PeterL1n/RobustVideoMatting v1.0.0, sha256-pinned) into the app-data matte dir, as a background job (returns {job_id}; progress via the jobs domain). onnxruntime rides the PERCEPTION venv (so for anyone who's set up perception the install is just the model). With `path`: BROWSE-to-existing — point at an rvm.onnx already on disk (validated + persisted, synchronous). On success the doctor `matte` card flips missing -> ok. The runtime is invisible plumbing cutd manages (a one-shot CLI spawned per bake, like the perception sidecar) — one app, no second window. OPTIONAL — core editing + render work without it. RVM is GPL: we ship integration, the user installs the model on consent.

model.description: Which background-removal tier to install. Default rvm (portable, AUTOMATIC, license-clean, CPU-ok). matanyone = the PREMIUM opt-in (MatAnyone2 — NVIDIA, non-commercial, target-assigned, cleaner edges).

path.description: Browse-to-existing: a model file already on disk (rvm.onnx, or matanyone2.pth when model=matanyone). Omit to download.

accept_noncommercial.description: REQUIRED to download model=matanyone: explicit acceptance that the MatAnyone2 weights are NON-COMMERCIAL (NTU S-Lab License 1.0). Download happens on your consent and responsibility. Without it a download request returns an invalid_args licence notice. Browsing to an existing checkpoint does not require this flag.

verbs.result: rvm: NO path -> {job_id} (downloads the 14 MB RVM model); WITH path -> {model, source:'browse', doctor}. matanyone (needs accept_noncommercial:true): before starting a job or downloading, refuses a driver-reported sm_70 (Volta) card with invalid_args, a plain reason, cause and suggested_action to use Standard RVM; unknown generations are never refused. NO path -> {job_id} (builds an isolated torch 2.15.0 / torchvision 0.29.2 venv, cu132 on Windows/Linux and default-index on macOS, with its own setuptools>=84.1.0 floor; downloads 141 MB + 323 MB + 323 MB of models, plus several GB for tools; a failed MatAnyone2/SAM2 import probe fails the job; finish result {model, venv_python, uv_version, checkpoint, matanyone_ready:true, cuda_available, matte_premium_ready}); WITH path -> browse a matanyone2.pth. Flips the matte / matte_premium doctor card.
